targetText: nationalisation of the banks, which would not deprive any “owner” of a single kopek, presents absolutely no technical or cultural difficulties, and is being delayed exclusively because of the vile greed of an insignificant handful of rich people. If nationalisation of the banks is so often confused with the confiscation of private property, it is the bourgeois press, which has an interest in deceiving the public, that is to blame for this widespread confusion.
summary: Nationalization of banks does not mean immediate personal confiscation: it consolidates accounting and nationwide state control.
explanation: Lenin refutes bourgeois scaremongering that portrays state regulation and banking nationalization as immediate expropriation of personal possessions: nationalization unifies books, ends commercial concealment, and places credit at the service of social planning.
